amendments.normalized_body: Fix carbon conservation test failures caused by atmospheric CO2 gas exchange not being disabled. In `shrimp_feeding_pathway.rs::feeding_test_state()` and the equivalent high-mortality/reproduction budget test fixtures, set `state.process_params.reaeration_kla_base = 0.0` and `state.hardware.aeration.enabled = false` (or add an equivalent CO2-exchange-disable mechanism) so the chemistry system's Henry's law CO2 exchange does not inject or remove carbon from what are supposed to be closed-system conservation tests. Currently 4 tests fail because `system:chemistry` CO2 gas exchange adds/removes atmospheric carbon: `closed_system_shrimp_feeding_conserves_carbon` (+304 mg C over 7 days), `shrimp_mortality_transfers_reserve_to_detritus` (+584 mg C over 30 days), `test_high_mortality_200_hours_conserves_n_c_and_accumulates_detritus` (+1.46 mg C at hour 25), and `test_closed_system_shrimp_reproduction_conserves_n_and_c` (-3546 mg C over 60 days).

Add a runtime or test-time mechanism to disable CO2 gas exchange independently of O2 reaeration. Currently CO2 exchange is derived from `compute_o2_kla()` scaled by `KLA_CO2_TO_O2_RATIO`, so the only way to disable it is to zero `reaeration_kla_base` AND disable aeration, which also eliminates O2 exchange. A dedicated flag or coefficient (e.g., `co2_exchange_enabled: bool` or `co2_kla_scale: f64` defaulting to 1.0) on ProcessParams would let tests isolate the shrimp feeding loop while keeping O2 exchange if desired.

The `test_closed_system_shrimp_reproduction_conserves_n_and_c` test (budget_tracking.rs:686) has a tolerance of 1e-6 mg while running for 60 days with full algae/microbial/shrimp systems active. Even with CO2 exchange disabled, floating-point drift over 1440 hours with dozens of interacting subsystems will likely exceed 1e-6 mg. Either tighten the test to isolate just reproduction (disable non-shrimp systems) or widen the tolerance to match what multi-system 60-day conservation can realistically achieve (e.g., 0.1–1.0 mg).

Document that `reserve_g` grows without bound in Phase 1 and add a comment in the daily shrimp pipeline (shrimp.rs:step_daily_shrimp or route_consumed_food) noting the expected follow-up: maintenance respiration drain on reserve. Without a drain, multi-year simulations accumulate arbitrarily large reserves, which is biologically unrealistic and will cause the reserve pool to dominate the N/C budget. Consider adding a minimal maintenance drain (e.g., a fraction of reserve respired daily) as part of this bead rather than deferring entirely.

`crates/tank_core/src/budget_helpers.rs:227-248` adds `assert_o2_balanced`, but the check only proves `inventory_delta == sum(entry.net_mg())`; it never proves that the recorded oxygen `in_mg`/`out_mg` pairs are themselves correct. That is a real gap because snapshot-derived budgets still collapse oxygen to a single net delta (`crates/tank_core/src/types/budget.rs:81-85`), and stage recording only debug-asserts net consistency (`crates/tank_core/src/types/budget.rs:161-174`). The new regression at `crates/tank_core/tests/budget_helpers.rs:348-365` can therefore pass even if a stage regresses from correct gross O2 bookkeeping to a net-only or otherwise wrong gross split, which is exactly the class of bug this helper is supposed to guard against.

`crates/tank_core/tests/budget_helpers.rs:109-126` tries to isolate `TANK_BUDGET_DEBUG` with a mutex, but the mutex only protects callers that also take that same lock. The smoke test at `crates/tank_core/tests/budget_helpers.rs:389-395` sets a process-global environment variable and then runs under Rust’s default parallel test harness, so unrelated tests in the same integration-test process can execute `step_and_inspect()` while debug mode is still enabled. When I ran `cargo test -p tank_core --test budget_helpers -- --nocapture`, other tests emitted budget debug blocks while this guard was live. That makes the suite order-dependent and sets up future stderr/debug-path flakes.
